name: Guest JSON
description: What the guest's JSON surface reads, what it writes, and what it refuses to let across.

scenarios.title: Every JSON value reads as its native counterpart
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a document holding each JSON value kind
scenarios.then: each maps to its native type, with String keys

scenarios.title: A document need not be a container
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a bare JSON number

scenarios.title: Object members keep the order they were written in
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses an object whose members are not in sorted order
scenarios.then: the resulting Hash carries them in the document's order

scenarios.title: Malformed input is refused
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a document that is not JSON

scenarios.title: The guest may carry on past a parse failure
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code rescues the parser error and returns a value

scenarios.title: An integer that fits stays an integer
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses the largest value the guest's Integer width holds

scenarios.title: A small negative integer stays an integer too
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a small negative integer

scenarios.title: An integer past the width widens rather than wraps
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a value one past the guest's Integer width

scenarios.title: A widened integer is still exact where a Float can be
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses the largest integer a Float represents exactly
scenarios.then: it yields that value as an exact Float

scenarios.title: An integer too large to represent is refused, not rounded
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses an integer beyond exact Float representation

scenarios.title: A JSON real reads as a Float
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a JSON real

scenarios.title: Exponent form is a real like any other
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a real written in exponent form

scenarios.title: Asking for Symbol keys gets them at every level
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a nested document asking for symbolized names
scenarios.then: every object at every level is keyed by Symbols

scenarios.title: Keys are Strings unless asked otherwise
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a document without asking for symbolized names

scenarios.title: Asking for Strings explicitly gets Strings
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a document asking for symbolized names to be off

scenarios.title: An option is read by its name, not by its spelling
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a document passing the symbolize option under a String key

scenarios.title: Symbolizing touches keys and nothing else
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a document with String values asking for symbolized names

scenarios.title: Native values write as compact JSON
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a structure of native values

scenarios.title: A control character is written as its escape
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a String holding control characters
scenarios.then: each appears as its JSON escape

scenarios.title: What was escaped reads back as what it was
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses back what it generated from a String needing escapes

scenarios.title: A Symbol is written as its name
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a structure using a Symbol as key and as value
scenarios.then: each appears as that Symbol's name

scenarios.title: An Integer key is written as a String
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a Hash keyed by an Integer
scenarios.then: the key appears as that Integer's string form

scenarios.title: A Float key is written as a String too
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a Hash keyed by a Float
scenarios.then: the key appears as that Float's string form

scenarios.title: A key that is not a scalar has no string form to take
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a Hash keyed by a container

scenarios.title: A number JSON cannot write is refused
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a Float that is not a finite number

scenarios.title: A String that is not text is refused
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a String whose bytes are not valid text

scenarios.title: A Symbol whose name is not text is refused as well
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a Symbol whose name is not valid text

scenarios.title: An Array subclass is written as an array
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from an instance of an Array subclass

scenarios.title: A Hash subclass is written as an object
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from an instance of a Hash subclass

scenarios.title: A String subclass is written as a string
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from an instance of a String subclass

scenarios.title: Pretty printing indents, and leaves empty containers alone
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code pretty-prints a structure holding empty containers
scenarios.then: it emits the indented layout with those containers inline

scenarios.title: Pretty printing changes the layout and not the document
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses back what it pretty-printed

scenarios.title: An object opts in by saying what it is
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from an object whose opt-in hook answers a native value

scenarios.title: What the opt-in hook answers is encoded like anything else
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from an object whose opt-in hook answers a structure

scenarios.title: An object that never opted in is refused
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a plain object

scenarios.title: Only the opt-in hook opts an object in
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from an object that overrode the other serialization method instead

scenarios.title: Parsing at the depth bound succeeds
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a document nested to the bound

scenarios.title: Parsing past the depth bound is refused
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code parses a document nested one level past the bound

scenarios.title: Generating at the same depth bound succeeds
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a structure nested to the bound

scenarios.title: Generating past the depth bound is refused at the same depth
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
scenarios.when: guest code generates from a structure nested one level past the bound

scenarios.title: Parsing produces data, never a capability
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary with a Service bound
scenarios.when: guest code parses a document shaped like a capability reference

scenarios.title: A capability reference has no JSON form
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
guest code holding a capability reference
scenarios.when: it generates from that reference

scenarios.title: Nesting a capability reference does not hide it
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
an object whose opt-in hook answers a structure holding a capability reference
scenarios.when: guest code generates from that object

scenarios.title: Using a capability reference as a key does not hide it either
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
a Hash keyed by a capability reference
scenarios.when: guest code generates from that Hash

scenarios.title: Asking a capability reference to serialize itself stays in the guest
given: a Sandbox over the JSON-capable Guest Binary
guest code holding a capability reference
scenarios.when: it calls the opt-in hook on that reference
scenarios.then: the raise happens in the guest without reaching the host

text: Reading and writing JSON is compute the guest does on its own, so the
scenarios follow what each direction produces and, more importantly, what
each refuses. A value with no JSON form is refused rather than approximated:
an integer too large to represent exactly, a number that is not finite, bytes
that are not text, a key that is not a scalar.
The boundary scenarios are the reason this surface can be offered at all.
Parsing yields data and never a capability, whatever the document is shaped
like; generating refuses a capability reference wherever it sits — bare,
nested inside what an object opted in, or standing as a key — and refuses it
in the guest rather than by asking the host what to do with it.
